items.title: UN condemns deadly wave of drone strikes in war-torn Sudan
items.summary: Drone strikes killed and injured dozens across Sudan on Monday as the ongoing war continues to cause soaring displacement and hunger.

items.title: ‘Season of fear’: Escalating Israeli attacks on West Bank olive farmers, deadly strikes on Gaza
items.summary: Israeli attacks on war-torn Gaza over the weekend killed at least six Palestinians, including children, despite a year-old ceasefire agreement. Meanwhile, in the occupied West Bank, settler violence continued through the ongoing olive harvest, with UN independent experts on Monday urging Israel to protect Palestinian farmers.

items.title: The Yemen War, Saudi-Iran relations and Another Escalation in the Gulf
items.summary: This week on Hold Your Fire!, Richard speaks with Crisis Group experts Yasmine Farouk and Hamidreza Azizi about the war in Yemen, attacks on Saudi Arabia, Iran’s strategy and implications for Gulf security and diplomacy over the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Sudan conflict: Peace efforts resume to end ‘drone war’ fuelling humanitarian crisis
items.summary: Talks to halt the fighting in Sudan and alleviate the humanitarian crisis there continued in Geneva on Wednesday, where nearly two dozen countries convened to discuss a pathway to a ceasefire and transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people.

items.title: ‘One step away from famine’: Inside Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
items.summary: Following extreme hunger warnings, a bitter reality is unfolding across Afghanistan: food is available, but remains inaccessible for millions of people.

items.title: Yemen war continues to force families from homes amid hunger and disease
items.summary: More than 250,000 people have now fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the UN said on Tuesday, citing particular concern for those sheltering in the southwestern city of Taiz and the wider governorate, where access is “essentially blocked”.

items.title: Iran’s enriched uranium re-emerges as point of contention in US talks
items.summary: Iran's nuclear enrichment has emerged as a major point of contention amid diplomatic push to end the war.

items.title: Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 73 security recruits, local authorities say
items.summary: Three missiles hit a camp in government-controlled Shabwa province on Monday that was being used as a training centre, Yemen's army says.

items.title: Guidance: TF RAID Avengers: AI swarming competition
items.summary: The Rapid AI Delivery Taskforce (TF RAID) is running a competition to access Ukraine’s Avengers Labs platform to enhance autonomous drone swarming and collaborative drone operations.

items.title: As Sudan war spills into Central African Republic, UN warns against early peacekeeper exit
items.summary: The UN warned on Tuesday against a premature withdrawal of its peacekeepers as the war in Sudan spills over into the Central African Republic (CAR).

items.title: Trump and Zelensky at loggerheads despite new optimism
items.summary: The Ukrainian leader's hug with Steve Witkoff in the Norwegian capital is unlikely to dispel misgivings about US policy towards his country, writes Paul Adams.

items.title: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
items.summary: The two top tennis pros married in 2021 and have one child together.

items.title: Blast heard in Yemen’s Aden as Houthis claim attack on military camp
items.summary: Smoke seen rising near airport in Aden as Houthis say they attacked a military camp with a ballistic missile.

items.title: Drone attack in disputed Sudan-South Sudan border region kills at least 153
items.summary: South Sudan authorities say Sudan's army launched drone attack on market, as MSF says it is treating 20 wounded people.

items.title: How War is Reshaping Iran’s “Axis of Resistance”
items.summary: Three years of hostilities have transformed Tehran’s network of allies in the Middle East. The Islamic Republic is now relying more heavily on itself, while adapting its relationships with partners whose diminished military utility has not necessarily reduced its commitment to their protection.

items.title: Ukraine under Strain: The Choices Facing the EU
items.summary: As Russia’s war in Ukraine drags on, Kyiv faces mounting challenges and European support is increasingly critical. In this excerpt from the EU Watch List 2026 – Autumn Edition, Crisis Group explains how the EU and member states can aid Ukraine and help advance diplomatic efforts.

items.title: Haiti: Elections on hold as gangs adapt to security crackdown, Security Council hears
items.summary: Armed groups in Haiti are adapting to intensified security operations, stepping up reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas, the UN warned the Security Council on Monday.

items.title: Gaza: Funding cuts leave half a million without food assistance
items.summary: Funding shortages have forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash assistance to hungry families in the Gaza Strip by roughly one third – a move that will affect some 500,000 people as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday.

items.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
items.summary: A truck carrying people to a funeral and a market alleged to be supplying fuel to the RSF were targeted.

items.title: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line
items.summary: The serviceman was surrounded by landmines and enemy drones so a ground rescue was not possible, Ukraine's military says.

items.title: Global warming will breach 1.5°C – but deep, fast cuts can still bring it back
items.summary: With global temperature rise set to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels, countries “must pull out all the stops” and urgently cut emissions to minimize the overshoot and return to the internationally agreed threshold by the end of this century.

items.title: AI on track to ‘crowd out’ human decision-making in warfare
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is already being widely used on the battlefield, and the role of human judgment in military operations is shrinking rapidly, the head of the UN’s independent disarmament research institute warned on Tuesday.

items.title: Hunger is ‘an avoidable tragedy’ in a world of plenty: Türk
items.summary: More than a quarter of humanity struggles to get enough food, even though the world produces enough for everyone, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday, blaming injustice and the denial of human rights for hunger in a world of plenty.

items.title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge
items.summary: The lawsuit argues the White House exceeded its authority in imposing the latest tariffs on the country and caused "immediate harm to American businesses".

items.title: How Israel’s war on Lebanon has cost young people with autism and ADHD
items.summary: Experts warn that war takes a heavy toll on neurodivergent people, who often rely on routine.

items.title: Are the UK, France being pulled into the Saudi-Houthi conflict?
items.summary: The European states say their support for Riyadh is 'defensive', but analysts warn Houthi reaction may complicate that.

items.title: Israeli soldiers mock Lebanese home they rigged with explosives
items.summary: Israeli soldiers in Southern Lebanon are seen ‘jokingly’ giving a tour of a displaced family’s home.

items.title: Hegseth Lauds New American Golden Age During Arsenal of Freedom Tour Stop
items.summary: During the second of two stops on his Arsenal of Freedom tour, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth praised the progress the U.S. and its defense industrial base have made over the past two years under President Donald J. Trump's administration.

items.title: Hegseth Praises Ohio Aerospace Workers During Arsenal of Freedom Tour
items.summary: In the first of two stops on his Arsenal of Freedom tour, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth thanked Ohio aerospace workers for working with a warfighter's urgency.

items.title: Arctic Experiment Explores Ways to Close Air Surveillance Gaps
items.summary: U.S. military personnel, scientists and international partners conducted live-fly testing in Alaska during the final event of a three-year Arctic air domain awareness experiment series, collecting data to assess technology that could help close surveillance gaps across the state.

items.title: Engineering Squadrons Fortify Pacific Airfields, Advance Agile Combat Employment
items.summary: Air Force civil engineers revitalized historic runways and infrastructure abandoned after World War II on Tinian, Northern Mariana Islands, helping prepare the Pacific theater for future operational requirements.
